why: I went through each verifier PASS and FAIL condition and checked it against its line. None is stricter than its line. Check 1 asks only that the output matches the `<path>:2: ` form followed by "an error text", so no exact wording is required. Check 2 asks for exit 2 and stderr that is "non-empty". The extra items (lockfile, shebang, CRLF, JSON.parse message) sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)". There is no branch-name rule, mutation test or limit on which files the PR may touch. The behaviour lines are checked by running the program: Check 1 and Check 2 run the CLI on temp files, Check 3 imports and calls lint(), and Check 4 runs `npm test` as well as reading the tests. Check 6 runs `npm ci && npm test` and reads the workflow check. Reading files only is used for lines that are about files: package.json fields, test coverage and READMEs. Neither must_not item is broken.
